### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**12** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validatePatch))_
- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validatePatch))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validatePatch))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via LifecycleService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`  _(via LifecycleService (symbol, a top-level class), retention_overrides (literal, a string literal in GOVERNANCE_MAP_KEYS; a string literal in LEGACY_TEXT_NOT_APPLIED_KEYS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validatePatch))_
- `content/docs/frontend/cli.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validatePatch))_

- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via LifecycleService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validatePatch))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via LifecycleService (symbol, a top-level class), retention_overrides (literal, a string literal in GOVERNANCE_MAP_KEYS; a string literal in LEGACY_TEXT_NOT_APPLIED_KEYS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via LifecycleService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validatePatch))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via retention_overrides (literal, a string literal in GOVERNANCE_MAP_KEYS; a string literal in LEGACY_TEXT_NOT_APPLIED_KEYS))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via invalid_type (literal, a string literal in validatePatch))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cb589e93abba7f8f61cfb9692daecbe6235ed46f` — the merge of head `fcafa11dda483eae6554253a1c86bbe0e80d4966` into base `cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cb589e93abba7f8f61cfb9692daecbe6235ed46f && git checkout cb589e93abba7f8f61cfb9692daecbe6235ed46f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b fcafa11dda483eae6554253a1c86bbe0e80d4966 && git checkout -B drift-repro cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b && git merge --no-ff fcafa11dda483eae6554253a1c86bbe0e80d4966

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cba7d8ae719f22e80ae7b336e4ee3a15d5c3057b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Head-sha: `e4d9a02a4d`

**CHANGES · in-seat review (no spec / skills / ADR hunk, so no Fable round) · 2026-11-07T22:03Z**

I read the whole diff: `settings-service.ts` (`jsonShapeMiss` at both doors), `lifecycle-service.ts` (`governanceMap`), `SettingsView.tsx` (`parseJsonDraft` / `outgoingSettingsPatch` / the `json` pre-save block), the changeset, the `config-resolution.mdx` paragraph, and the three new test files. The door and the console halves meet the card.

**should-fix — legacy text under `retention_overrides` must not start deleting rows on upgrade without an admin acting.** `governanceMap` applies every stored string that parses to an object, for all three keys. For `quotas` / `quota_defaults` that is safe: they only raise `quota-exceeded` alerts and never delete (`lifecycle-service.ts` header, "quotas/growth never delete data"). `retention_overrides` drives the reaper, which batch-deletes rows past `maxAge` / `expireAfter`. Today a deployment holds such text dormant, and the default windows are in force. With this PR, the first sweep after the upgrade would start deleting on a window nobody has looked at since the old console swallowed it. The changeset's "check them before you upgrade" asks every operator to read a release note before an irreversible effect, and the seat does not accept that trade.

Fix: keep the read-side repair for `quotas` and `quota_defaults` (warn once, apply). For `retention_overrides`, a stored string is **not** applied. Log it once at `error`, naming the key and the one-step fix: open Setup → Data Lifecycle and Save. The console already shows the stored text in the textarea, and a Save now sends the parsed object, so the admin's Save is the explicit consent. Pin it: a legacy string under `retention_overrides` deletes nothing on a sweep, and the same value saved as an object does. Ablate the guard. Rewrite the changeset's "Values saved as text before this release" paragraph to match.

**Accepted as reported:**
1. `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx` is added to the file surface. The paragraph it amends is falsified by this PR for `json` keys.
2. The ADR-0087 marker sits in the changeset, and the PR body states the disposition in prose. This is accepted, provided the PR-body guards are green on the next head.
3. The PR body's line 2 uses the card thread's own link.
4. Console type-check is left to CI's Type Check UI. The ACCEPT waits for it to be green.
5. Text that parses to a non-object (`42`) passes the console and is refused by the server's `invalid_type` on that row. That is acceptable.

Gates as reported: 100/100 derived exit 0 with `--ran` reconciled; `pnpm lint` 0; full dogfood 435 passed / 3 skipped, VERDICT 0; 6 negative pins ablated. The next head re-runs the derived gates. The narrowing is unchanged by the fix, so the dogfood run is not owed again unless the diff grows beyond `lifecycle-service.ts`, its test and the changeset.

## Contract review

Head-sha: `c4ad13974762e3b1622c0d40a1b623e9449c8709`

**CHANGES · in-seat delta r2 · 2026-11-07T22:35Z**

Round 1's should-fix is resolved in code. `LEGACY_TEXT_NOT_APPLIED_KEYS = {retention_overrides}`: `governanceMap` returns `undefined` for that key's legacy text with one `error`, while quota text still applies with one `warn`. The global pair and the organization pair are pinned (no 1d reap and no organization pass from text; both appear from the object), and the guard ablation reds 2/8. The changeset and the PR body (rewritten by the seat at the dev's request) match.

**should-fix — the remedy the logs print cannot be performed as written.** Both the `error` (retention) and the `warn` (quotas) tell the admin to open Setup → Data Lifecycle and "save the page once". The console only offers Save when `draft` has a key (`SettingsView.tsx` `dirtyKeys.length > 0` gates the save bar, and `onSave` returns on an empty draft). Opening the page and saving therefore sends nothing, so the stored text stays text, and the retention window never applies.

Fix: make the printed remedy true and pin it. The seat prefers the console half: when a `json` key's resolved value is a string, not locked, the page treats it as needing a save. It seeds that key's draft with the stored text, so the save bar shows one unsaved change, and a short inline note says the value was stored as text and will be saved as an object. A Save then sends the parsed object through `outgoingSettingsPatch`. Pin it: a stored string under a `json` key shows the save bar on load, and Save PUTs the object. The fallback, if that is not workable, is wording in both log lines and the changeset that names an edit to the value before saving. Either way, send me the PR-body lines to change and the seat rewrites them.
